title: El ritmo español de comer
summary: Spain's meal rhythm — desayuno, comida, cena, merienda — and the tradition of la sobremesa

blocks.title: Three meals, a Spanish schedule
blocks.body: Spain's meal clock runs later than most places: **el desayuno** (breakfast) is quick and light — coffee and something sweet. **la comida** is the day's big meal, around 2pm. **la cena** (dinner) is light and late, around 9 or 10pm. In between, many people have **la merienda**, an afternoon snack.
blocks.callout: Careful: **la comida** means both 'food' and 'lunch' in Spain — context tells you which.

blocks.title: La sobremesa
blocks.body: After eating, nobody rushes off. **La sobremesa** is the after-meal chat at the table — coffee, maybe a drink, conversation that can run longer than the meal itself. It's one of the most Spanish habits there is.

blocks.title: El día a día de la comida

pairs.note: Spain eats later — and dines even later.
A Madrid restaurant kitchen might not open for dinner until 8:30pm — completely normal.

blocks.prompt: What time do people in Spain typically have la cena (dinner)?
blocks.explain: Spanish dinner runs late compared to most countries — usually between 9 and 10pm.

blocks.prompt: Type the Spanish word for Spain's big midday meal (not 'el almuerzo').
blocks.hint: Same word as 'food' — context tells you which.
blocks.explain: *la comida* is Spain's big midday meal, eaten around 2pm.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type what you hear.
blocks.speak: la cena es a las diez
answers: la cena es a las diez

blocks.scene: Lucía explains the Spanish meal rhythm to you over coffee

lines.speaker: Lucía
lines.nl: Mira, aquí desayunamos poco: un café y ya está.
lines.en: Look, here we eat little for breakfast: a coffee and that's it.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: ¿Y la comida fuerte es a mediodía?
lines.en: And the big meal is at midday?

lines.speaker: Lucía
lines.nl: Sí, sobre las dos. Y luego, sobremesa, o sea, un rato charlando.
lines.en: Yes, around two. And then, sobremesa — I mean, a while chatting.

lines.speaker: Lucía
lines.nl: Tarde. A las nueve o las diez, tranquilamente.
lines.en: Late. At nine or ten, no rush.

lines.speaker: You
lines.spotlight: A first taste of *me gusta* — the full lesson is tomorrow.
